Enriched pathways for a set of proteins

Source: R/enrich_pathways.R
enrich_pathways.Rd

Runs pathway/GO enrichment on a set of protein (gene) identifiers using the gprofiler2 package (an internet connection is required) and returns a protein → pathway mapping that can be used as a row annotation for plot_heatmap(..., pathway_annotation = TRUE).

Usage

enrich_pathways(
  proteins,
  organism = "hsapiens",
  sources = NULL,
  p_cutoff = 0.05,
  ...
)

Arguments

proteins

Character vector of protein/gene identifiers (e.g. gene symbols such as "IL6", "CD40").

organism

Organism used by gprofiler2::gost() (default "hsapiens").

sources

Optional character vector of gprofiler2 data sources (e.g. "GO:BP", "KEGG", "REAC", "WP"). If NULL, the gprofiler2 defaults are used.

p_cutoff

Significance threshold for enriched pathways (default 0.05).

...

Additional arguments passed to gprofiler2::gost().

Value

A data.frame with one row per (protein, pathway) pair for the significant enriched pathways, with columns Protein, Pathway, term_id, source and p_value (sorted by p-value). Returns NULL (with a message) if gprofiler2 is unavailable, no internet connection is available, or no significant enrichment is found.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
enrich_pathways(c("IL6", "CD40", "IL10", "TNF", "CCL2", "CXCL8"))
} # }
